Upstream: PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp PRs #217 (Hadamard MTP fix) and #218 (PTQ1_0 kernel); branches pr-ptq1-mmv and pr-hadamard-mtp on github.com/sudoingX/llama.cpp, stacked branch bonsai2. All numbers measured on one RTX 3060 12GB (sm_86, CUDA 12.4, driver 550.144.03) on 2026-09-18/19 unless a path says otherwise. Target box this reading serves: local-town RTX 2070 SUPER 8GB, cc 7.5 (sm_75), 16 threads, driver 595.84, measured here with nvidia-smi 2026-09-20 06:24.
summary: bonsai2-small-gpu makes PrismML's Ternary Bonsai 2 27B (Qwen3.8-27B, PTQ1_0 ~1.75 bpw ternary, 5.95 GB) usable on consumer cards. Four artifacts: (1) serve/8gb.sh, the 8GB tier line, -c 65536 -ngl 99 -fa on -np 1 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --jinja, ~7.3 GB VRAM (measured on a 12GB card; the 8GB row is explicitly PENDING in serve/README.md). (2) A 1.5x decode kernel: the pr-ptq1-mmv branch of the PrismML fork (5 commits on prism 9a9394a89; also patch series kernel/patches/kernel/0001..0005), fixing the fork's PTQ1_0 mat-vec by planar-transposing q8_1 activations and giving every thread work. On an RTX 3060 12GB: tg128 26.32 -> 40.47 tok/s (1.53x), pp512 unchanged ~268, VRAM unchanged; gain shrinks with depth (1.42x@16K, 1.25x@64K, 1.16x@131K). (3) The Qwen 3.8 MTP head grafted back for --spec-type draft-mtp: extract_head.py + merge.py on unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf, plus a 15-line qwen35.cpp Hadamard fix for the lean file. Draft acceptance 0.85-0.95 code, 0.73-0.81 bash, 0.45-0.68 prose. On the prebuilt fork n-max 1 is +8% (25.0->27.1); with the kernel branch flag-off 39.8 and n-max 1 50.1 tok/s, lossless only with GGML_CUDA_BATCH_INVARIANT=1. (4) sweeps/rtx3060.md, one card only. The 8GB tier is the documented-but-unrun one; the reproduction risk is VRAM (7266 MiB served vs 7786 MiB usable on this 2070 SUPER, ~520 MiB headroom) and sm_75 vs the tested sm_86. The fork's prebuilt sm_75 binary and the sha256-verified 27B segments are ALREADY on this box, so only concatenation + the container run is needed for the prebuilt path; the 1.5x kernel needs a source build with -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75.
key_facts: MEASURED (serve/8gb.sh, sha256 7d005cd1cb9391dd4b4da187121826fd7b4c342e84be8ee43fb7943a3d7e9afd): the 8GB serve line verbatim is `llama-server -m "${1:-Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf}" -c 65536 -ngl 99 -fa on -np 1 -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 --jinja --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8899`. Offload split: -ngl 99 = every layer on GPU, no CPU offload; -np 1 = one slot.

MEASURED (serve/README.md): the tier table says 8GB tier context 65536, served VRAM 'about 7.3 GB', notes 'the Hermes floor; measured on 12GB, 8GB row pending'. The 12GB+head line is -c 131072, 10.6 GB, and needs the merged file from graft/.

MEASURED (results/KERNEL_REPORT.md, KERNEL_REPORT section 6 and sweeps/rtx3060.md): patched build, original file, flag off, -np 1, q4_0 K/V on RTX 3060 12GB: 65536 context = 7,266 MiB idle / 7,284 after a 120-token answer; 262144 = 11,682 / 11,700. The kernel adds no VRAM (the planar activation buffer replaces the q8_1 buffer).

MEASURED (README.md): 'The file skips 6GB cards, the weights alone are 5.95 GB; on 8GB the 64K line is the one to try.' Parent file Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf = 5,946,648,928 bytes, sha256 53107f530aa52eb00912263ab1ee29bd199261c87cd7b4ad4ca1318c1fe33ee3.

MEASURED (README.md, results/KERNEL_REPORT.md, kernel/PR_KERNEL.md): the 1.5x kernel is the pr-ptq1-mmv branch of github.com/sudoingX/llama.cpp, 5 commits on top of prism/prism 9a9394a89 (files ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq-ptq1_0.cuh, mmvq.cu, quantize.cu, tests, mmvq/mmvf/fattn). RTX 3060 12GB, llama-bench r=3, original file: tg128 26.32 -> 40.47 tok/s (1.53x); pp512 269.6 -> 267.8 (unchanged). Depth gain: 1.53x@0, 1.42x@16K, 1.25x@64K, 1.16x@131K. Build: `cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86 -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build -j` (use 75 on the 2070 SUPER).

MEASURED (sweeps/rtx3060.md): with the MTP head and the kernel branch at 131072 context on the RTX 3060, flag off 39.8 tok/s, --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 1 with GGML_CUDA_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 = 50.1 tok/s median (code 53.2, prose 41.8, bash 50.1) and greedy output byte-identical to flag-off on all three prompts; n-max 2 lossless 45.4, default kernels 48.7 (not identical). On the PREBUILT fork (no kernel branch) n-max 1 is only +8% (25.0 -> 27.1) and greedy is NOT identical.

MEASURED (results/RUN_REPORT.md, results/MODEL_CARD.md, kernel/PR_HADAMARD.md): the MTP graft needs Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf + the 15 blk.64.* tensors of any Qwen3.8-27B GGUF (unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf, 16,464,440,224 B, sha256 322e194ff79741c7baa497c240f677f54b201b0efab44ca8e50f122b39123482). Draft acceptance on RTX 3060: code 0.85-0.95, bash 0.73-0.81, prose 0.45-0.68, 0.56-0.65 at 41.8K context. Fat merged file 7,012,820,512 B / 867 tensors, lean 6,297,658,848 B / 866 tensors. VRAM with head: 10,638 MiB (fat, prebuilt) / 9,956 MiB (lean, patched) at 131072; max context 163840 (prebuilt) / 196608 (patched lean).

MEASURED (this box, nvidia-smi 2026-09-20 06:24): GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 SUPER, 8192 MiB total, compute capability 7.5, driver 595.84, CUDA 13.2; the running workload is a stock ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda container (6742 MiB used, 97% util) which per the README cannot load PTQ1_0. Host nvcc is 12.0.140 and supports compute_75.

MEASURED (this box, /data/ml/llama-prism-fork/fork/llama-prism-b10685-7dffb15): the PrismML prebuilt CUDA fork (tarball sha256 29326793ab8a8d0b42d348bcd0ba0a5f4513220d29d1a1d40e943e357c666386, 260,792,089 B) is already extracted; libggml-cuda.so.0.21.0 contains 145 'sm_75' SASS matches and 340 'ptq1_0' matches, so the PREBUILT path needs no build on this card.

MEASURED (this box, /data/ml/models/bonsai): the 27B PTQ1_0 file exists as 12 segments (seg000-seg011); `cat seg* | sha256sum` = 53107f530aa52eb00912263ab1ee29bd199261c87cd7b4ad4ca1318c1fe33ee3, exactly the pin. No single .gguf is assembled yet. Free disk on /data = 238 GB.

MEASURED (agi context, .agi/context/local-maxxing/bonsai/vram_budget.md, 2026-09-18): on this 2070 SUPER the usable VRAM is 7786 MiB; the 27B header shows block_count 64, full_attention_interval 4 (only 16 of 64 layers carry KV), 65536 B/token f16 KV, weights 5671 MiB; at -c 8192 the weights+KV sum is 6183 MiB and 32768 would OOM. The 8gb.sh line's 64K with q4_0 KV measures 7266 MiB on the 3060, leaving ~520 MiB of this card's 7786 MiB.

ESTIMATE (no benchmark run on the 2070 SUPER; derived from the 3060 numbers and spec bandwidth 360 GB/s for the 3060 vs 448 GB/s for the 2070 SUPER, and sm_75 vs sm_86): patched pr-ptq1-mmv decode ~38-52 tok/s at empty context and ~12-18 tok/s at 64K filled; prebuilt fork ~28-35 tok/s empty and ~9-13 tok/s at 64K. Marked ESTIMATE: the kernel is partly latency-chain bound, not purely bandwidth bound, and it was never compiled or run for sm_75.
reusable_assets: serve/8gb.sh — the verbatim 8GB serve line (ctx 65536, -ngl 99, -fa on, -np 1, -ctk/-ctv q4_0, --jinja, temp 1.0/top-p 0.95/top-k 20, port 8899). The same file on this box only needs the 27B gguf path.

kernel/patches/kernel/0001..0005 — the PTQ1_0 planar-transposed layout, dedicated mat-vec kernel, Bonsai 2 perf shapes, GGML_CUDA_BATCH_INVARIANT, and the bf16 under-64-row rule; git-am onto prism/prism 9a9394a89. (Recipe step 7 says 0001..0006 but only 0001..0005 exist.)

kernel/patches/0001-qwen35-mtp-hadamard-inverse.patch / kernel/patches/hadamard/0001-*.patch — 15 lines in src/models/qwen35.cpp applying llama_mul_mat_hadamard + signs to the MTP token-embedding lookup; needed for the lean (no embedding copy) merged file, saves 682 MiB and unlocks 196608 context.

graft/tools/gguf_raw.py, extract_head.py, merge.py (+ --strip round trip), tests/ — pure-Python, no GPU, no extra packages; copies tensors as opaque byte spans so PTQ1_0/PQ2_0 sizes are never decoded. Merge(strip(x)) reproduces the original sha256 byte for byte.

graft/tools/batch_numerics.py — replays a prefix at batch sizes 1,2,3,4,8 and reports next-token logprobs; the tool that proved the fork's kernels are not batch-invariant and that BATCH_INVARIANT=1 makes 1..4 bit-identical. Directly reusable to verify any 2070 SUPER build.

graft/tools/deep_probe.py, probe.py, verify_identity.py — throughput (client tok/s), deep-context and greedy-identity harnesses; results/identity/*.json holds 300-token transcripts and per-token logprobs.
sweeps/rtx3060.md + CONTRIBUTING.md — the measured RTX 3060 row, the depth/context ladders, and the exact llama-bench command template for adding a 2070 SUPER row.

On this box already: /data/ml/llama-prism-fork/fork/llama-prism-b10685-7dffb15 (prebuilt sm_75 fork with ptq1_0 kernels) and /data/ml/models/bonsai/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf.seg000..011 (sha256-verified, 5.95 GB).
failures_and_lessons: The 8GB tier is documented but NOT measured: serve/README.md marks the 8GB row 'pending' and 8gb.sh comments 'measured footprint about 7.3 GB (on a 12GB card; 8GB row pending)'. 7266 MiB served vs 7786 MiB usable leaves ~520 MiB on a headless 2070 SUPER; any display or second GPU process OOMs it.

The kernel was built and tested only for sm_86 (RTX 3060). This card is sm_75; the report's reverted tensor-core experiments used mma.sync.m16n8k16.s8 (Ampere-class), but the kept dp4a kernel should compile for sm_75. The build flag must be -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75, not 86.

Stock llama.cpp (including the ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda container running on this box) loads the Q2_0 variant as gibberish and rejects PTQ1_0; the PrismML fork is mandatory. The prebuilt fork was already extracted here, so no build is needed for the base path.

Greedy identity fails on the PREBUILT fork: flag-off vs flag-on text diverges after 14-52 tokens at near ties because PTQ1_0 CUDA kernels are batch-size dependent (up to ~0.1 nats). Only pr-ptq1-mmv + GGML_CUDA_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 makes 1..4-column batches bit-identical; even then batches 5..8 differ by up to 0.03 nats (top-1 unchanged) and prompt processing (MMQ at 9+ tokens) is not invariant.

n-max 2/3 lose on the prebuilt fork because a 3-token verify batch costs 2.4 single-token passes on PTQ1_0; even 0.9 acceptance cannot pay. n-max 1 is the only setting that beats flag-off there. With the kernel branch, lossless n-max 2 loses at depth because the invariant vector flash-attention kernel is slow over 42K keys (21.1 vs 22.2 tok/s flag off).

The per-column ratio targets (pp2/3/4 = 1.15/1.30/1.50) were missed: 1.22/1.55/1.84. Two correct tensor-core attempts (redundant-decode and cooperative-decode mma) and a third permuted-decode experiment were all 1.2-2.4x slower than dp4a at 2-4 columns and were reverted; the residual is the dependent 16-byte load chain per (block,column).

ncu could not run in the container (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM); attribution was done with a temporary cudaEvent hook. Also: pkill -f llama-server once killed the issuing ssh session (the pattern matched the script itself); use pkill -x. A stray C-c during a 41.8K prefill left the server alive but unresponsive.
Recipe step 7 says 'Apply results/kernel/patches/0001..0006' but the series has only 5 patches (0001..0005); the KERNEL_REPORT's original work branch had 7 commits. Minor doc inconsistency.

The MTP head was trained against fp16 hidden states but reads a ternary trunk here; acceptance is high on code (0.9) and much lower on prose (0.5), and the head costs 1.2-1.9 GB VRAM, which alone exceeds the 8GB tier's ~520 MiB headroom at 64K. MTP is a 12GB-tier feature, not an 8GB one, unless context is cut to a few K.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The pr-ptq1-mmv PTQ1_0 kernel compiles and runs on sm_75 (RTX 2070 SUPER) and gives at least 1.3x the prebuilt fork's tg128 on the original Bonsai 2 27B file at 65536 context.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Build fails for compute_75, or ptq1_0 MUL_MAT correctness cases fail on the card, or patched tg128 < 1.3x prebuilt.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Read-only prep: `cat /data/ml/models/bonsai/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf.seg* > /data/ml/models/bonsai/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf`, sha256 against 53107f53...; clone github.com/sudoingX/llama.cpp pr-ptq1-mmv; inspect the patch for sm_86-only intrinsics (grep for mma.sync.m16n8k16.s8 / __nv_ in the kept kernel). GPU build+bench needs the card.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: $0 GPU hours if the card is free; ~30 min build (16 threads) + 5 min bench; ~6 GB disk for the assembled gguf (238 GB free).

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The verbatim serve/8gb.sh line (-c 65536, -ngl 99, q4_0 K/V) loads Ternary Bonsai 2 27B fully on GPU on this 2070 SUPER without OOM, within the ~7786 MiB usable VRAM.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: cudaMalloc OOM or CPU offload appears in the load log, or nvidia-smi shows weights spilled to host RAM.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Arithmetic-only pre-check using the on-disk budget (weights 5671 MiB + measured 3060 KV 1472 MiB/64K + compute) vs 7786 MiB; assemble the gguf and read its header; no GPU needed until the load test.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: $0; assembly is a local cat + sha256 (~12 s), the load test needs the GPU free of the current 9B server.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The grafted Qwen 3.8 MTP head cannot be served at 64K on the 8GB tier because the lean head adds ~1.2 GB (fat ~1.9 GB) over the ~7.3 GB flag-off footprint, but it fits at <=8-16K context.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: nvidia-smi shows the head resident at 65536 context under 8192 MiB, or acceptance/speed measured there.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Budget arithmetic from results/RUN_REPORT.md VRAM rows (base 5810 MiB + 1472 MiB/64K + 1229 MiB lean head) against 7786 MiB usable; no GPU required to produce the predicted OOM.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: $0 for the arithmetic; the confirmatory load needs the card and the merged file.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 makes greedy output with --spec-draft-n-max 1 byte-identical to flag-off on this card too, so the MTP speedup is a lossless claim rather than a throughput-only one.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: verify_identity.py compare shows any divergence at temperature 0 over 300 tokens, or batch_numerics.py shows N=1 vs N=2 logprob differences above noise.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run graft/tools/batch_numerics.py against a running server and diff results/identity transcripts; the tool is pure Python and needs only a live endpoint.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: $0 compute if a server is up; otherwise gated on the GPU load test.

open_questions: Does the PrismML prebuilt libggml-cuda.so's 145 sm_75 matches actually include the PTQ1_0 path exercised by Bonsai 2, or only PQ2_0? The 340 'ptq1_0' string matches suggest yes but that is a string count, not a run.

What is the real tg128/pp512 of the original Bonsai 2 27B file on this specific 2070 SUPER, patched vs prebuilt, at -c 65536 with q4_0 K/V? No 27B row exists on this card; only the 1.7B PQ2_0 row (pp512 6892.8 / tg128 317.9 tok/s, -ngl 99 -t 16) is measured.

Does the 8gb.sh line fit under 8192 MiB total with the headless display driver overhead, or does it need -c 32768 or a smaller KV type? The 3060 measured 7266 MiB against this card's 7786 MiB usable; the 8GB row is still 'pending'.
Will the dp4a kernel build for compute_75 with nvcc 12.0 (host) given the report used CUDA 12.4, and does the planar-transposed q8_1 layout need any sm_80+ feature?

Is there any measured 2070 SUPER / sm_75 row in the town's bench/ dir that would let us replace the ESTIMATE with MEASURED? Only sweeps/rtx3060.md exists in the source repo; the town's own local-maxxing bench dir was not inspected for Bonsai rows beyond the 1.7B.

The kernel/patches/kernel series is 5 patches but recipe step 7 says 0001..0006; was a 6th patch dropped when the work branch (7 commits) was rebased into the PR series (5 commits), and does the missing patch matter for reproduction?
